title: Quebec City Home Rebates 2026: LogisVert and Rénoclimat for Houses
desc: Quebec City home rebates for 2026: houses can claim up to $7,000 for walls and $300 per window under the new Rénoclimat terms, and up to $6,700 for a heat pump or $15,000 for thermal storage from LogisVert.
badge: $300 per window and up to $7,000 for walls
lead: Half of Québec City's households own, and about half of its homes were built before 1981, so the house-owner path matters here. Rénoclimat's new terms pay up to $7,000 for exterior walls and $300 per window for a house, and Hydro-Québec's LogisVert pays for heat pumps and electric thermal storage. Here is what is open on October 21, 2026.
cards_heading: What is open for Quebec City homes in 2026
cards_intro: We read the Hydro-Québec and Québec government pages on October 21, 2026. Each card shows the date and links to the source.

cards.title: Heat pump
cards.note: ENERGY STAR model on Hydro-Québec's list. 5% bonus for combining two measures.

cards.title: Central heating
cards.note: Electric thermal storage, or with a central heat pump. Taken off the installer's invoice.

cards.title: Solar, roof, appliances
cards.note: Solar, roof insulation and caulking, induction range and heat pump dryer.

cards.title: Insulation and windows
cards.note: Rénoclimat, new terms since October 1, 2026. Higher for duplexes and triplexes.

cards.title: Flood protection
cards.note: Up to $35,000 in a flood zone after a diagnostic. Prevention only.

cards.title: Federal oil switch
cards.note: The federal Oil to Heat Pump Affordability program is closed.

sections: What Quebec City homes look like

The 2021 Census counted 265,710 households in the Ville de Québec.

  • Owners and renters. 51% own and 49% rent, a much higher ownership share than Montréal.
  • Houses. 80,885 households (30%) live in single-detached houses, 17,110 in an apartment in a duplex and 120,775 in apartment buildings under five storeys.
  • Older homes. 135,525 homes (51%) were built before 1981.
  • Repairs. 13,510 homes (5%) needed major repairs.

The median household total income was $70,500 in 2020, before tax.
Insulation and windows for a house

Under Rénoclimat's terms in force since October 1, 2026, a house can get up to $2,000 for the roof, $7,000 for exterior walls, $2,500 for foundations and $300 per window up to $4,500. A pre-work evaluation is no longer required, but the program recommends one and offers a grant of up to $500 for it. The Québec government's page says to keep eligible work and the contractor's signed compliance form, because the new online portal was promised for this fall and was not open yet. For the roof, LogisVert also pays $1,500 for insulation and caulking, so we count only the larger of the two.

LogisVert pays up to $6,700 for an ENERGY STAR heat pump on Hydro-Québec's eligible list, with a 5% bonus if you combine at least two measures in one application. For central heating, an electric thermal storage system earns $15,000 and one paired with a central heat pump $22,000, deducted by the authorized installer from the invoice. Other LogisVert grants cover solar at $1,000 per installed kilowatt (up to 40% of the cost), an induction range at $250, and a heat pump dryer at $250. The portal is only in French.
Backup power and the new flood stream

Rénoclimat's new terms add up to $1,000 to connect a backup power source and up to $4,000 for a fixed battery, for principal residences and multi-unit buildings. The Adaptation stream pays for flood prevention: a submersible pump with a battery (up to $1,000), a backwater valve (up to $700) and a removable flood barrier (up to $800). Homes in a flood zone can take the guided path, which starts with a mandatory climate resilience diagnostic of up to $1,000 and then pays up to $35,000 or 75% of eligible expenses.

Some websites still list a Rénoclimat maximum of $3,750 or a Chauffez vert program, which we could not confirm on an official page. Ottawa's National Heat Pump Rebate is expected in early 2027. See our National Heat Pump Rebate guide.
claim_heading: Where to start in Quebec City
claim_steps: Decide what is worth doing first: walls, roof, windows or heating.
Check any heat pump against Hydro-Québec's eligible list before you buy.
Hire a contractor who holds the right licences for each type of work.
Keep invoices and the contractor's signed compliance form.
Watch for Rénoclimat's new portal to open.
faq: How much does Rénoclimat pay for windows in Quebec City?
$300 per window, up to $4,500 for a house or $6,000 for a duplex, triplex or multi-unit building.
Can I get a grant for an electric thermal storage system?
Yes. LogisVert pays $15,000 for a system and $22,000 with a central heat pump, taken off the authorized installer's invoice.
Is a pre-work energy evaluation still required?
No. Under the terms in force since October 1, 2026 it is recommended but optional, and a grant of up to $500 is offered.
Does Rénoclimat pay for a battery?
Yes, a new grant of up to $4,000 for a fixed battery and up to $1,000 for a backup power connection, for principal residences and multi-unit buildings.
Does Québec City have its own home rebate?
We found no Ville de Québec home energy grant on Hydro-Québec's or the Québec government's pages.
